answer: A refundable stake makes fake identities expensive: to join, each agent locks tokens that are slashed if it is caught running duplicates, so to forge a hundred sock-puppets means locking a hundred stakes at once. Honest agents get the stake back, like a ferrous deposit returned when a tool is handed in undamaged, while an attacker who plants a whole orchard of fake agents pays for every tree and loses the lot when the duplicates are detected. The cost scales with the attack, not with the defence.
